_meta.purpose: The three allow-list sets that decide whether a token may stand in a physical name, plus the order in which they are consulted.
_meta.shape: Three flat arrays plus "consult_order". They map one-to-one onto the approved_abbreviations, common_keywords and short_full_words arguments of GovernedDictionary.

_notes.consult_order: TOTAL is deliberately in two sets. The order above makes it report as a common keyword, not a short full word. Both readings are defensible, which is the point: the order has to decide, and a test can see that it did.
_notes.entry_less_members: MGMT, MSG and SVC are approved abbreviations with no dictionary row. They exercise the allow-list-with-no-entry rule: the token is known and approved, and its expansion is the token itself rather than a long form. Fifteen of the short full words (BATCH, CITY, CLASS, CYCLE, EMAIL, GRADE, LEVEL, LIMIT, PLAN, SCORE, TERM, TITLE, TOTAL, YEAR, ZONE) and every common keyword are entry-less for the same reason.
_notes.proper_nouns_excluded: ZIP, ABA, ATM, NDS and GLX are approved physical forms but are not listed here. They are approved through their keep_as_abbrev dictionary rows, so a compliance verdict for them can carry the proper-noun reason code instead of the generic approved-abbreviation one. Adding them here would hide that distinction.
_notes.unapproved_tokens: CUSTMR, ACCNT, TRANS, AMNT, NUM, DTE, PYMNT and EFFCTV appear in no set here and carry keep_as_abbrev false. They are the corpus's unapproved tokens: known, expandable, and not permitted to stand in a physical name.
